title: Lurker Magazine - Metal, Punk, Outsider Art, Tabletop games and RPGs
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AUG114ir5eQ

A flip-through of the first three issues of Lurker, prompted by a Patreon giveaway. Daniel (@dungeondive) met two of its creators at Dungeon Siege West, where he ran Escape the Dark Castle and Darklight: Memento Mori and one of them got a seat at the Darklight table.

The pitch is metal, punk, outsider art and tabletop games in one perfect-bound black-and-white object substantial enough to feel like a trade paperback — about twenty dollars an issue, which he thinks is fair for something made purely out of passion. His own credentials surface here: he ran the book department at Tower Records and managed one of the largest magazine racks on the west coast, and this is the kind of thing he would have stocked.

Each issue carries a bonus. Issue one came with a 7-inch. Issue two came with a complete solo game from the Cave Evil team — a siege scenario adapting William Hope Hodgson's *The House on the Borderland*, fold-out map, cut-your-own cards and chits. Issue three, the giveaway copy, carries an RPG module plus a novella set in the Cryptic Explorers world.

Inside: a Cave Evil interview, Satanic Mojo Comics, original serialised fiction, a history of the Ouija board, and reviews of Super Blood Harvest, Escape the Dark Sector and a sword-and-sorcery anthology written entirely by members of heavy metal bands. Issue three also carries a full-spread article on DungeonQuest, written and photographed by Daniel himself.

----

Daniel pays twenty dollars an issue partly to keep a small underground press alive. What is the one publication you'd still buy on paper?
